title: Fasting for bodybuilding & how to maintain and make gains during Ramadan/Lent
summary: NH explains that fasting works for fat loss only because it builds a calorie deficit, that muscle loss during fasting is overblown, and that fasting's real value is spiritual and for controlling appetite. For Ramadan he advises training in the morning a few hours after a pre-dawn meal of watery carbs and salted water, and breaking the fast with protein and vegetables before carbs while avoiding junk. For Lent, don't replace animal protein with excess carbs. The goal is to keep momentum without stressing about progress.
claims: Everyone fasts to some extent; NH usually goes 12-14 hours between bedtime and his first meal
Meal timing is individual; no single method fits everyone
Lifters need two things: pre-workout meals that sustain effort and post-workout meals that sustain recovery
The body has reserves and knows how to use them; it won't fall apart because you aren't eating
'Starvation mode' is mostly an excuse, though there is some truth to how the body handles a big refeed
Fasting causes fat loss only because skipped meals add up to a deficit; a normal calorie deficit does the same
A calorie deficit is a 'volume fast' and fasting is a 'frequency fast'; both are just deficits
Claims that fasting boosts fat metabolism or growth hormone are bogus or negligible; its real benefit is mental toughness and easier calorie control
You won't lose gains from fasting; supplement companies created the fear of not constantly eating
Carb powders sell for about 10 times the price of the foods they're made from
The body attacks fat before muscle because fat is energy-dense and easily replaced while muscle is expensive and vital; true autophagy of muscle only comes deep into starvation
Muscle loss from fasting comes from training performance dropping, not from the fast itself
Eating the instant you feel hunger trains bad habits and leads to overeating; waiting lets appetite match intake or even leave you in a deficit
If a deficit hurts your sleep, fast during the day and eat a big meal before bed; sleep matters more than the hunger
He was raised going to bed hungry and can sleep on an empty stomach
With full-day fasts, schedule training on days when you're fed and energetic
Fasting helped him rein in an appetite that ran wild after he over-bulked
If you struggle to eat enough calories, fasting is not for you
The spiritual side of fasting (humility, self-control through controlled suffering) should stay central
During Ramadan, train in the morning about 2-4 hours after the pre-dawn meal, not at night when you're depleted
Pre-dawn meal before training: carbs such as soft (not al dente) pasta or sticky rice that hold lots of water, a glass of water with a pinch of sea salt, and salted cooking water
Prep the pre-dawn meal the night before; if needed, wake around 4 a.m. to eat, sleep again, and train around 6 a.m.
If morning training is impossible, train at lunch; avoid training late in the afternoon or evening when you're dehydrated
Training in the morning frees the rest of the day for the spiritual side of Ramadan
Break the fast with protein and good fats first, then fill up on carbs like pasta or couscous
Many people gain fat and lose muscle and strength during Ramadan by eating junk and training at night; aim for maintenance, not a surplus
Night-time protein shakes are fine if protein intake falls short
Eat plenty of vegetables and salads during Ramadan for water and micronutrients; feeling foggy points to a micronutrient shortfall
For Lent, plant proteins like beans, or whey if allowed, replace animal protein; don't overdo carbs and sugar
Ideally you end a fasting month at the same weight or lighter
During Ramadan or Lent, keep a 'cruise control' training momentum instead of stressing about progress, to avoid restarting from scratch afterwards
Nobody should be pressured into fasting; not everyone has the strength of mind for it
